chapter: Porch interview and Jazz Train plans
title: Never had lessons; learning piano by listening
summary: He had few lessons, learned at a friend's school and a professor's piano down the block, and by listening.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you take piano lessons when you were a kid?
Oh, a long time ago. (Inaudible.) Didn't sit too well with me.
Didn't sit too well with me, either.
(Inaudible.) So that's the result of it.
I bet (inaudible) in your house, though.
No, ma'am. I went down to the school, a friend of mine, and played on that piano. Never had a piano, couldn't afford it.
Well, when you were a kid, --
(Inaudible) right down the block, two or three houses from where I lived. They had a beautiful piano because their father was a professor, he taught music. And he (inaudible).
When you were young, did you make up songs then?
No. No, I just listened to (inaudible). That's all I could do, boom, boom, and that's it. (Inaudible) lessons. I wasn't fortunate enough to take lessons. So I had to listen to the other (inaudible).
You learned to play piano by listening to other people. You never had lessons.
